A feedback cycle with no delay has no computable value: the prior would
be the very output being computed. Faust makes this unsayable by
inserting its delay implicitly; Mentl names the depth, so the depth can
be wrong, so the medium refuses it.

E_ZeroDelayFeedback is the eleventh armed class — armed at birth on the
literal licence (the depth is read from the authored `delay(<int lit>)`
at the site, no resolution dependency, wheel census 0). Both the `delay`
and `Delay` spellings convict; a computed depth answers false rather
than guessing. Gate seen RED: the identical program ran, exit 30.

Two kills came first, both from the artifact, both before a byte moved:

The banked Iterate-class membership predicate ("the loop-driving resume
grade IS the class") classifies no clock. Measured by badge, `choose` is
the wheel's only `->*` op; tick, advance_sample, sample_rate,
current_sample, yield, result and iter_context are every one `->1`,
because a clock handler advances state and resumes ONCE per tick — the
iteration is the caller's loop. §4④ unifies search, sampling,
backtracking and the clock as one substrate, not one cardinality. The
predicate would have fired E_FeedbackNoContext at all thirteen wheel
`<~` sites; the no-false-refusal control refused it.

The reverse-edge prerequisite had no referent: register_effect_ops
already env_extends the effect name with EffectDeclKind(op_names) at the
same one writer, and `mentl where` already reads it.

E_FeedbackNoContext therefore keeps zero construction sites on purpose,
and SYNTAX now says why: a `<~` prior is a per-site register advanced by
the enclosing fn's next call, which is why bandpass_step needs no row.
The honest form is the inferred clock, Phase 8's tier.
